prerequisites: Previous knowledge of basic concepts regarding the general laws of rigid body mechanics and their subsequent application to solving engineering problems is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Identify and quantify the different types of efforts, stresses, and deformations.
Dimension and check simple mechanical elements.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering aimed at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, electrical and electronic installations, energy installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling learning of new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, and other similar tasks.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge and application of the principles of strength of materials.

syllabus_topics: Basic Concepts of Elasticity. Failure Criteria
Simple Stresses: stresses, deformations, and diagrams.
Combined Stresses: stresses, deformations, and diagrams.
assessment_rules: For Continuous Evaluation in the Ordinary Call, the Final Grade is calculated as 0.80 * Exam Grade (out of 10) + Continuous Evaluation Grade. Continuous evaluation includes 0.5 points from 5 lab practices (0.1 each) and 2 short theoretical-practical controls (0.75 each). For the Extraordinary Call, the Final Grade is 0.90 * Exam Grade (out of 10) + 0.50 * Continuous Evaluation Grade, where half of the continuous evaluation grade is considered. Differentiated Evaluation consists of a 100% theoretical-practical written exam.
